rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Test temperature-dependent selectivity while holding the gradient fixed, targeting the tightly clustered middle peaks. The current last peak is comfortably below 10 minutes, allowing selectivity exploration without a time penalty.

Back off slightly from 55 C to recover separation in the newly critical middle pair, while using a shallower gradient to spread the central cluster. The available retention-time margin should accommodate this longer gradient without a time penalty.

Raise temperature at the shallower gradient to improve the remaining central close pair. The increased separation around the earlier middle peaks may preserve their resolution at 55 C, with the last peak still below 10 minutes.

At 55 C, the critical later pair was slightly better resolved with the steeper gradient, while the earlier pair benefited from the shallower gradient. An intermediate 12-minute gradient may bring both above R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
Injection 5 has reached the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark. Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether all peaks can elute sooner while preserving full resolution.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope to recover the R = 1.29 pair while retaining the higher starting organic fraction. This may restore full resolution with an elution time close to or slightly shorter than the maximum-score benchmark.

Retain injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore lower-temperature selectivity with the shorter gradient. Cooling may separate the central cluster on a different elution-order branch, enabling full resolution in less time.

Test a faster, hotter gradient for an alternative selectivity window, potentially moving the critical middle pair through an elution-order crossover. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback if this faster method sacrifices resolution.

Use a slightly shallower gradient to spread the hot-run central cluster, while raising the starting organic fraction to adjust its selectivity. This tests a faster alternative to injection 5, which remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Refine around the maximum-score method with a slightly shallower gradient, aiming to improve the R = 1.59 pair without pushing the R = 1.52 pair below threshold. This tests the robustness of full resolution while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Refine injection 7 by lowering the endpoint one step to bring its R = 1.47 pair above threshold while preserving the other critical pair. This seeks a second fully resolved operating window; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Preserve injection 5’s gradient slope and temperature while shortening the programmed gradient to 10 minutes. Since all peaks previously eluted before this gradient ends, full resolution and the maximum CRF should be retained.

Raise temperature one step from the fastest fully resolved method to test whether retention can be shortened without losing full resolution. This isolates the temperature effect at the successful gradient slope; injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Return to 55 C and test a higher-start, shallower gradient near the fully resolved injection 14. This may improve the minimum-resolution margin while retaining CRF 1.000; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Slightly steepen the fully resolved injection 14 gradient to shorten retention while testing its resolution margin. The proposed slope lies between injection 14’s successful slope and injection 7’s marginally unresolved slope.
